evidence: Ov. Met. 3.588: ars illī sua cēnsus erat
terms.comment: Skill in making or doing something, and the craft itself; a skill is ars, skills artēs. Skilled in, perītus with the genitive (see experience).
Traupman’s word for skill; skilful is artificiōsus (Traupman 158, 380).

evidence: Cic. ND 2.123: māchinātiō quaedam atque sollertia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Quick, inventive skill; also spelled sōlertia (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sall. Jug. 46.8: locōrum et mīlitiae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Skill that comes of experience; Sallust and Tacitus, not Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Ars illī sua cēnsus erat. Cum trāderet artem, «accipe quās habeō, studiī successor et hērēs,» dīxit «opēs.»
phrases.english: His skill was his whole fortune. When he handed it on, he said: “Take what wealth I have, my successor and heir in the trade.”

phrases.latin: memor artificiī meī vetus frīgidae cultor mittō mē in mare
phrases.english: mindful of my skill, an old devotee of cold water, I throw myself into the sea

sources: Lewis & Short: ars · Lewis & Short: artificium · Lewis & Short: sollertia · Lewis & Short: peritia
